title: Do diversity and context collapse kill an online social network?
abstract: Our social lives consist of various circles, such as family, friends, and colleagues. Differences in norms and expectations among these circles can create tension in large online social networks (OSNs) due to blurred boundaries. It is unclear whether this phenomenon, known as context collapse, outweighs the convenience of having diverse communities in one place for OSN users. To explore this trade-off, we examined if ego network characteristics indicating context collapse could explain users' decisions to leave iWiW, a defunct Hungarian OSN with over 3.5 million active users at its peak.
